stem: Short-term memory (STM) is best described as which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: A permanent memory store with vast capacity
options.misconception: Confuses the temporary short-term store with long-term memory.
options.explanation: A permanent memory store with vast capacity is long-term memory; short-term memory is temporary and limited.

options.label: B
options.text: A split-second register of raw sensory impressions
options.misconception: Confuses short-term memory with the sensory register that feeds it.
options.explanation: A split-second register of raw sensory impressions is sensory memory, which feeds short-term memory rather than being it.

options.label: C
options.text: A store of learned motor skills and habits
options.misconception: Confuses a temporary store with long-term procedural memory.
options.explanation: Learned motor skills and habits are procedural memories held in long-term implicit memory, not in a temporary store.

options.label: D
options.text: A temporary store processing input from sensory memory
options.misconception: None — STM temporarily holds and processes what sensory memory passes on.
options.explanation: Short-term memory is a temporary storage system that processes incoming sensory memory, handling what the sensory register passes on.

options.label: E
options.text: A store of personal experiences tied to time and place
options.misconception: Confuses a temporary store with long-term episodic memory.
options.explanation: Personal experiences tied to time and place are episodic memories, a kind of long-term explicit memory.

context: Learning objective: Short-term memory is a temporary storage system that processes incoming sensory memory.
